vBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2325: gitignore + untrack .pan/test/result.json so it stops causing a guaranteed merge conflict on every merge

plan.title: bug(pipeline): .pan/test/result.json tracked at a shared path → guaranteed merge conflict on EVERY merge (gitignore it)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: `.pan/test/result.json` is the test role's deterministic verdict artifact — written by the test role prompt (src/lib/cloister/test-agent-queue.ts:44) and read back host-side FROM THE WORKSPACE by recoverTestVerdictHostSide (src/lib/review-status.ts:661). It is workspace-local recovery state that never needs to travel through git, but it is NOT gitignored, so it is tracked and committed on main at a single fixed path. Every feature branch's test role writes its own verdict to that same path and commits it, so main and every branch always differ → a guaranteed merge conflict on every merge, for every issue (PAN-2265 hit it repeatedly during RUN-55). Verified: `git ls-files` shows it tracked, `git check-ignore` exits 1 (not ignored), `git show origin/main:.pan/test/result.json` returns content.
narratives.Proposal: Treat `.pan/test/` like the other ephemeral per-run Overdeck runtime dirs already in .gitignore (.pan/events/, .pan/convoy/, .pan/prompts/, .pan/pid/, .pan/feedback/): add `.pan/test/` to .gitignore and `git rm --cached .pan/test/result.json` in one atomic bead. Then add a regression guard test proving the path stays ignored+untracked and that host-side recovery still resolves a written workspace file. Recovery reads the on-disk workspace file, not git, so gitignoring does not affect it.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Do NOT change the test role prompt (test-agent-queue.ts step 8) — writing .pan/test/result.json is correct and must stay.
- Do NOT change any runtime recovery logic in review-status.ts or test-verdict.ts — it already reads the workspace path correctly.
- Do NOT touch or delete the two tracked `.pan/review/pan-*-uat.md` files — they are uniquely named per issue, not a shared-path recurring conflict, and are out of scope.
- Do NOT use `git rm` (working-tree delete) — only `git rm --cached` (index-only); the test agent still needs the file on disk.
- Do NOT retroactively rewrite history or remove the file from past commits.

autoDecisions.summary: Gitignore the whole `.pan/test/` directory, not just result.json.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches the existing ephemeral-runtime pattern (.pan/events/, .pan/convoy/, .pan/prompts/, .pan/pid/, .pan/feedback/) and satisfies AC #4 for any future sibling artifact written under .pan/test/.

autoDecisions.summary: Combine the .gitignore add and `git rm --cached` untrack into ONE bead.
autoDecisions.rationale: Neither half leaves the tree working+fixed alone — gitignore-without-untrack still conflicts; untrack-without-gitignore is re-added on the next test run. It is a single atomic fix.

autoDecisions.summary: Add the regression guard to the existing test-verdict.test.ts suite.
autoDecisions.rationale: That suite already exercises readTestVerdictArtifact/clearTestVerdictArtifact; the ignore+recovery guard belongs alongside it rather than in a new file.

expected_outputs: git ls-files .pan/test/result.json prints nothing (no longer tracked)

narrative.Action: In .gitignore, add a `.pan/test/` line to the existing 'Overdeck runtime artifacts (ephemeral, not tracked)' block (currently .gitignore lines 138-146, alongside .pan/events/, .pan/convoy/, .pan/prompts/, .pan/pid/, .pan/feedback/). Then run `git rm --cached .pan/test/result.json` to stop tracking it WITHOUT deleting the working-tree file (index-only — the test agent still writes/reads it on disk). Commit both changes together. Do NOT use plain `git rm`. Do NOT modify the test role prompt or any recovery logic.

items.title: Given the .gitignore change, when `git check-ignore .pan/test/result.json` runs, it exits 0 and prints the path (the file is now ignored).
After `git rm --cached`, `git ls-files .pan/test/result.json` returns empty output — the file is no longer tracked — while the file still exists in the working tree on disk.
`git status --short` in the workspace shows the test verdict artifact as ignored (absent from status), not as modified or untracked-and-listed.
The .gitignore rule covers the whole `.pan/test/` directory (not only result.json), so any future artifact written under .pan/test/ is also ignored; `git ls-files '.pan/test/*'` returns empty.
Regression test: verdict artifact stays ignored+untracked and host-side recovery still resolves it

narrative.Action: Add regression cases to src/lib/cloister/__tests__/test-verdict.test.ts that lock the fix: (1) a guard asserting `.pan/test/result.json` is git-ignored at the repo root — e.g. run `git check-ignore -q .pan/test/result.json` (exit 0) and assert `git ls-files .pan/test/result.json` is empty, so a future re-track fails CI; (2) a recovery case asserting that after a workspace file is written, `readTestVerdictArtifact(workspace)` still returns the parsed {status,notes} verdict — proving gitignoring does not break host-side recovery. Reuse the existing suite's temp-workspace helper (it already does `mkdirSync(join(ws, '.pan', 'test'), { recursive: true })`).

items.title: A new test asserts `git check-ignore` reports `.pan/test/result.json` ignored and `git ls-files` returns it untracked; the test fails if the file is ever re-tracked or the ignore rule is removed.

A test writes a verdict file into a temp workspace's .pan/test/result.json and asserts readTestVerdictArtifact(workspace) returns the parsed {status:'passed', notes} — proving host-side recovery still resolves the workspace artifact.
`npx vitest run src/lib/cloister/__tests__/test-verdict.test.ts` passes with the new cases and no pre-existing case in the file regresses.
